children.text: Slow mornings, and the case for doing one thing

children.name: Label · E1 · Inside the address bar

children.text: The puzzle moves into the address field, next to the star: extensions act on the page you are on, so they sit with the page. Click it for the list. The row keeps just ← address → ⬇ ⋮.
Slow mornings, and the case for doing one thing

children.name: Label · E2 · A rail on the right edge

children.text: E2 · A rail on the right edge
Nothing in the row at all. Push the pointer to the right edge (or press Alt+X): a slim rail of extension icons slides out over the page, then hides again. A faint handle shows where it lives.
Slow mornings, and the case for doing one thing

children.name: Label · E3 · A dock in the bottom-right corner

children.text: E3 · A dock in the bottom-right corner
A small round button floats in the corner of every page. Hover it and it opens into a row of extension icons, like the new tab page's dock. It fades to almost nothing while you scroll or read.
Slow mornings, and the case for doing one thing

children.name: Label · E4 · At the top of the menu

children.text: E4 · At the top of the menu
No extension button: the ⋮ menu opens with your extensions as a row of icons above the usual items. One click more than now, but the row is the calmest it can be.
Slow mornings, and the case for doing one thing

children.name: Label · E5 · With the site, in its address chip

children.text: E5 · With the site, in its address chip

Extensions are about the page, so they live in the page's own chip at the start of the address bar, next to its permissions: the ones active here, with what they did ("3 ads blocked"). The others are under Manage.
